title: The birth
hookLine: families give thanks with Japji and Ardas when a child arrives
tomorrow: how can a baby's name begin on a page of the Granth?

cards: A text at dawn: one photo, a tiny fist, a lot of exclamation points. Then the phone doesn't stop. In a Sikh family, the first words after news like that are often thanks.
Japji, the morning's first bani, said for the new life. An Ardas of gratitude. And a pot of karah prashad, made and shared with everyone who waited.

teach.h: ANG 396: THE TRUE GURU SENT THE CHILD.
teach.b: The Granth has a hymn of joy for a birth, Guru Arjan's, on ang 396. In paraphrase: the True Guru has sent the child; the long-lived one is born, as destined.
He came to dwell in the womb, and the mother's heart is full of joy.
The child is a gift sent, and the first answer to a gift is thanks, before plans, before names, before anything else.

teach.h: THE WEEK, BACK IN YOUR HANDS.
teach.b: Now the week, back in your hands. A shared lunch, a small langar: share the plate. Rehras at dusk, the morning's question come back: the day put down.
Kirtan and Lalo's bread at home: home fills up.
Sohila, the sky as the plate: sleep in praise. Daily words, a weekly sangat, regular seva: a rhythm for the week. Then a crib in its box, and Ardas: waiting with prayer.
And now the thing all that waiting was for.
A new life, met first with thanks.

how: When a child is born, Sikh families give thanks with Gurbani, often Japji, and an Ardas of gratitude, and share karah prashad; later the family brings the baby to the gurdwara, where the name is chosen from the hukam.

o: a ceremony where the baby is given its first turban
a fast the family keeps for the baby's first days
a new child met first with thanks, Japji and Ardas

games.q: two weeks of living it — tap the pairs.
p: the True Guru has sent the child

s: Sikh families wait until the naming before giving any thanks
the first words after a birth are often thanks: Japji, Ardas, karah prashad.
Guru Arjan's hymn on ang 396 rejoices at a child sent by the True Guru
and the mother's heart is full of joy.
Rehras opens with the same question as Japji's So Dar
what is that door? at dusk, the day is put down there.

games.q: a coworker texts the team a photo of her newborn. you want to mark it the way this lesson describes. what fits?
o: send warm thanks for the news, and bring in something sweet to share.
hold off on any reply until the baby has been given a name.
tell her which prayer her family ought to say for the baby.
games.why: a gift is first answered with thanks, and something sweet shared with everyone who waited, the way karah prashad is.

practice: Count, on your fingers, the people whose arrival in your life you're glad of: born into it, married into it, or befriended. For each one, say thank you, silently or out loud. Let the sit hold the last one.

wordCard.voice: The birth. A new child met with thanks: Japji, an Ardas of gratitude, and karah prashad for all.

orig.note: Punjabi: vadhaaee, congratulations: the word families send when a baby arrives.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: a new life, and someone new to live it with. Welcome, little one.
